name: A slash command teaches the Agent your design system
object: Skills in Framer: saved, reusable instructions (a design-system skill, a motion-system skill) that a team can invoke with a slash command to keep the Agent's output consistent
audience: design teams who use the Framer Agent often and are tired of repeating the same style rules in every prompt
message: This video tells design teams that a skill, written once, keeps the Agent on-brand every time you invoke it, instead of you re-explaining your rules in every chat.

moments.what: a chat panel shows a typed house rule, "use curly quotes," then kinetic type completes a second style rule mid-sentence, "...um, never light," implying a saved tone-of-voice or type rule
moments.copy: Use curly quotes... um, never light.

moments.what: a live site for a research-assistant brand, "helping teams do better research," shows its principles section being built out, matching the house style established a moment earlier
a prompt to create a new About page is typed with a slash command, /design-system, appended at the end, then a second clip shows /motion-system and /skills typed the same way
moments.copy: Create a new About page for the site, use /design-system.

moments.what: closes on the plain Framer glyph

cta: no spoken call to action; the film ends on the plain Framer logo mark right after the /skills command is typed
why: Showing the same slash command invoked across three different asks, quotes, a new page, motion, proves a skill is not a one-off trick but a rule the Agent will keep honoring every time it's called.
